claims: method_n132_n157/README.md says the folder holds the code that produced the packings in n132/ and n157/ and the high-precision solutions behind the two certificates, in four steps: a growth step (grow.py, surgery.py) that cuts the packing along one vertical and one horizontal line, moves the parts about 1.15 apart, copies every square in the layer next to a cut once across it (axis-aligned squares by one unit, tilted squares by 1/cos(theta) along the cut's normal) and drops a copy that overlaps another square by more than 0.15; an optimization (slp.py, nlp.py) that removes overlaps with linear programs at a fixed side and then minimizes the side with IPOPT through CasADi under wall constraints and one separating-axis constraint per corner of each pair of nearby squares; a high-precision solution (newton.py) of the contact equations by Newton's method at 900 bits with python-flint, one equation for each corner within 1e-6 of the edge line of a neighbouring square on a separating axis and one for each corner within 1e-6 of a wall, 1407 for n = 132 and 2024 for n = 157; and a certificate (package.py, mkcert.py) that scales the solution by 1 + 1e-60, shifts it by 1e-60, writes it as exact rationals and checks it in rational arithmetic.

method_n132_n157/README.md says that, run from the seed, the 109-square packing of best_fit_101_500.csv at Samanyu-dev/squares_in_squares 53551d7, by grow.py with cuts at x = 3.48, y = 8.61 and then x = 9.71, y = 3.33, newton.py and package.py, the scripts print the sides 11.976048386602 and 12.993302615406 after the two growth steps and write n132_exact.json and n157_exact.json byte for byte equal to the files in n132/ and n157/; it names Python 3.10 or later with numpy, scipy, casadi, python-flint, mpmath and matplotlib, and shapely for the second check.

n132_solution_250_digits.txt and n157_solution_250_digits.txt state the solutions of the contact equations to 250 decimal places: the side, then x, y and the angle in radians of each square. check_binary64.py (a separating-axis test over all pairs in binary64, least separation about -2e-15 at 132 and -4e-15 at 157) and check_shapely.py (the area of the union with Shapely, 132.0000000000 and 157.0000000000) read the exact JSON; the README says they were written for the folder and repeat the two checks reported with the packings, and that the perturbation trials and the force-balance check are outside the folder.

n132/n132_witness.yaml and n157/n157_witness.yaml at the pin add a softschema header naming packing.squares:Witness/v2 and this repository's witness.schema.yaml, a claim block (coordinate_provenance: verified, method: exact-algebraic, and limitations naming verify_exact.py and no optimality statement) and a lowercase id (W-n132-de-winter, W-n157-de-winter); the commit message says the squares and the sides are unchanged. The folder READMEs now call each file a Squares Project witness file (Witness/v2, center-basis, rational) and point to method_n132_n157/. The method README says the code was written with Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic) under the direction of Joost de Winter. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
